        "anchor": "stmt-prop-full-contiguity",
        "exact_quote": "Fix compactly nested regular boxes $Q\\Subset B$ in the interior of a $W$-flat domain, with fixed positive buffer ratios. Thus the complementary $N$ components are free. Let $\\mu_\\delta$ be its law and $\\pi_\\delta$ the plane law, restricted to the full spin pair in $Q$. The domains and any allowed exterior $(s,W)$ data may depend on $\\delta$, but their walls and prescriptions stay outside $B$. There is a uniform contiguity modulus: for every $\\varepsilon>0$ there is $\\zeta>0$ such that, for every sufficiently small mesh and every event $E$ determined by the full spin pair in $Q$, $$\\label{eq:spatial-contiguity}\n             \\pi_\\delta(E)<\\zeta\n           \\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n             \\mu_\\delta(E)<\\varepsilon.$$ The conclusion also holds if the tested data include $W$ in $Q$. In particular it applies to mesh-dependent tests. Either flat parity can be used by assigning $W$ to the parity carrying that flat wall. This statement does not include a fixed-color wired $N$ component before its removal.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-positive-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "The plane law is reflection positive across a row of corner-grid sites in each of the directions $0,\\pi/4,\\pi/2,3\\pi/4$. In its reflection Hilbert space, translation by two successive row spacings in the inward normal direction is a positive self-adjoint contraction. For the height-increment law, tangential translation by one row period is a commuting unitary. Reflection positivity and positive normal transfer remain valid for local spin and edge decorations strictly on one side of the row, and for independent uniform phase lifts of the height.         "exact_quote": "Partition finitely many local factors and pattern neighborhoods into two groups separated by a strict projection gap along one of the four reflection normals. Denote the result at lattice-normal-step translations by $M_\\delta(t)$. If $M_\\delta(t_\\delta)\\to0$ whenever $t$ belongs to some nonempty open interval of positive numbers and $t_\\delta\\to t$ is lattice rounded, then $M_\\delta(0)\\to0$.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-boundary-decay",
        "exact_quote": "Consider deterministic flat chambers in a fixed bounded region, with connected accessible walls, and a Hausdorff limit of their complements.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-conditional-flat-gff",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose a stopping exploration uses the cuts in <a href=\"#lem:finite-cuts\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:finite-cuts\">4</a>, so that, conditional on its revealed data $\\mathcal E_\\delta$, the unexplored chambers have independent flat laws with pairwise disjoint interiors. Let $R_\\delta$ be their centered unit-height remainders, patched by zero, and let $U_\\delta,F_\\delta$ be their open union and closed complement in $\\overline B_0$. Fix real tests $f_1,\\ldots,f_\\ell\\in C_c^\\infty(B_0)$, $u_1,\\ldots,u_\\ell\\in\\mathbb R$, and $d_0>0$. Put $$A_{\\delta,d_0}\n =\\left\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}\\left(\\bigcup_i\\mathop{\\mathrm{supp}}f_i,F_\\delta\\right)\\ge d_0\\right\\}.$$ Then $$\\begin{split}\n \\mathbb E\\Bigg[\\mathbf 1_{A_{\\delta,d_0}}\n \\Bigg|&\n \\mathbb E\\left[\\exp\\left(i\\sum_i u_iR_\\delta(f_i)\\right)\n                  \\,\\middle|\\,\\mathcal E_\\delta\\right]\\\\\n &-\\exp\\left(-\\frac1{2a^2}\n                  \\sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_{U_\\delta}(f_i,f_j)\\right)\n \\Bigg|\\Bigg]\\longrightarrow0.\n\\end{split}\n\\label{eq:conditional-flat-characteristic}$$ Here $G_{U_\\delta}$ is the continuum Dirichlet kernel of the resolved open chamber union, with zero covariance between its components.*\n\n\n*Multiplying the displayed difference by any uniformly bounded $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurable variable preserves the same estimate with its clearance indicator. To state the limiting consequence, let $\\mathsf E$ be a Polish space and let $e_\\delta$ be an $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurable $\\mathsf E$-valued variable. Suppose, for one fixed $s<-1$, that along a subsequence $$(e_\\delta,F_\\delta,R_\\delta)\\Longrightarrow(e,F,R)\n \\quad\\text{in }\\mathsf E\\times\\mathcal K(\\overline B_0)\n                   \\times H^s_{\\mathrm{loc}}(B_0),$$ where $\\mathcal K(\\overline B_0)$ is the space of nonempty compact sets with the Hausdorff metric. The limit $F$ is almost surely connected and contains $\\partial B_0$. Put $U=B_0\\setminus F$ and $$A_F=\\left\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}\\left(\\bigcup_i\\mathop{\\mathrm{supp}}f_i,F\\right)>0\\right\\}.$$ Then, almost surely, $$\\begin{split}\n &\\mathbf 1_{A_F}\\,\n \\mathbb E\\left[\\exp\\left(i\\sum_i u_iR(f_i)\\right)\n             \\,\\middle|\\,\\sigma(e,F)\\right]\\\\\n &\\qquad=\\mathbf 1_{A_F}\\,\n \\exp\\left(-\\frac1{2a^2}\n                \\sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_U(f_i,f_j)\\right).\n\\end{split}\n\\label{eq:conditional-flat-limit}$$ Thus, conditional on $\\sigma(e,F)$, the restrictions of $R$ to the component interiors of $U$ are independent zero-boundary GFFs divided by $a$, including components born from a pinched single precursor. This is first tested on deterministic compact buffers with positive limiting clearance and then extended by a countable exhaustion. The retained variable $e_\\delta$ may encode any exact-cut coordinates and flat constants for which this joint convergence holds; the constants are added after the centered assertion. Its $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurability excludes data from any later revelation.",
        "source_id": "PM-233.1"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-prop-conditional-flat-gff",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose a stopping exploration uses the cuts in <a href=\"#lem:finite-cuts\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:finite-cuts\">4</a>, so that, conditional on its revealed data $\\mathcal E_\\delta$, the unexplored chambers have independent flat laws with pairwise disjoint interiors. Let $R_\\delta$ be their centered unit-height remainders, patched by zero, and let $U_\\delta,F_\\delta$ be their open union and closed complement in $\\overline B_0$. Fix real tests $f_1,\\ldots,f_\\ell\\in C_c^\\infty(B_0)$, $u_1,\\ldots,u_\\ell\\in\\mathbb R$, and $d_0>0$. Put $$A_{\\delta,d_0}\n =\\left\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}\\left(\\bigcup_i\\mathop{\\mathrm{supp}}f_i,F_\\delta\\right)\\ge d_0\\right\\}.$$ Then $$\\begin{split}\n \\mathbb E\\Bigg[\\mathbf 1_{A_{\\delta,d_0}}\n \\Bigg|&\n \\mathbb E\\left[\\exp\\left(i\\sum_i u_iR_\\delta(f_i)\\right)\n                  \\,\\middle|\\,\\mathcal E_\\delta\\right]\\\\\n &-\\exp\\left(-\\frac1{2a^2}\n                  \\sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_{U_\\delta}(f_i,f_j)\\right)\n \\Bigg|\\Bigg]\\longrightarrow0.\n\\end{split}\n\\label{eq:conditional-flat-characteristic}$$ Here $G_{U_\\delta}$ is the continuum Dirichlet kernel of the resolved open chamber union, with zero covariance between its components.*\n\n\n*Multiplying the displayed difference by any uniformly bounded $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurable variable preserves the same estimate with its clearance indicator. To state the limiting consequence, let $\\mathsf E$ be a Polish space and let $e_\\delta$ be an $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurable $\\mathsf E$-valued variable. Suppose, for one fixed $s<-1$, that along a subsequence $$(e_\\delta,F_\\delta,R_\\delta)\\Longrightarrow(e,F,R)\n \\quad\\text{in }\\mathsf E\\times\\mathcal K(\\overline B_0)\n                   \\times H^s_{\\mathrm{loc}}(B_0),$$ where $\\mathcal K(\\overline B_0)$ is the space of nonempty compact sets with the Hausdorff metric. The limit $F$ is almost surely connected and contains $\\partial B_0$. Put $U=B_0\\setminus F$ and $$A_F=\\left\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}\\left(\\bigcup_i\\mathop{\\mathrm{supp}}f_i,F\\right)>0\\right\\}.$$ Then, almost surely, $$\\begin{split}\n &\\mathbf 1_{A_F}\\,\n \\mathbb E\\left[\\exp\\left(i\\sum_i u_iR(f_i)\\right)\n             \\,\\middle|\\,\\sigma(e,F)\\right]\\\\\n &\\qquad=\\mathbf 1_{A_F}\\,\n \\exp\\left(-\\frac1{2a^2}\n                \\sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_U(f_i,f_j)\\right).\n\\end{split}\n\\label{eq:conditional-flat-limit}$$ Thus, conditional on $\\sigma(e,F)$, the restrictions of $R$ to the component interiors of $U$ are independent zero-boundary GFFs divided by $a$, including components born from a pinched single precursor. This is first tested on deterministic compact buffers with positive limiting clearance and then extended by a countable exhaustion. The retained variable $e_\\delta$ may encode any exact-cut coordinates and flat constants for which this joint convergence holds; the constants are added after the centered assertion. Its $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurability excludes data from any later revelation.",

      "exact_statement": "Suppose a stopping exploration uses the cuts in <a href=\"#lem:finite-cuts\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:finite-cuts\">4</a>, so that, conditional on its revealed data $\\mathcal E_\\delta$, the unexplored chambers have independent flat laws with pairwise disjoint interiors. Let $R_\\delta$ be their centered unit-height remainders, patched by zero, and let $U_\\delta,F_\\delta$ be their open union and closed complement in $\\overline B_0$. Fix real tests $f_1,\\ldots,f_\\ell\\in C_c^\\infty(B_0)$, $u_1,\\ldots,u_\\ell\\in\\mathbb R$, and $d_0>0$. Put $$A_{\\delta,d_0}\n =\\left\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}\\left(\\bigcup_i\\mathop{\\mathrm{supp}}f_i,F_\\delta\\right)\\ge d_0\\right\\}.$$ Then $$\\begin{split}\n \\mathbb E\\Bigg[\\mathbf 1_{A_{\\delta,d_0}}\n \\Bigg|&\n \\mathbb E\\left[\\exp\\left(i\\sum_i u_iR_\\delta(f_i)\\right)\n                  \\,\\middle|\\,\\mathcal E_\\delta\\right]\\\\\n &-\\exp\\left(-\\frac1{2a^2}\n                  \\sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_{U_\\delta}(f_i,f_j)\\right)\n \\Bigg|\\Bigg]\\longrightarrow0.\n\\end{split}\n\\label{eq:conditional-flat-characteristic}$$ Here $G_{U_\\delta}$ is the continuum Dirichlet kernel of the resolved open chamber union, with zero covariance between its components.*\n\n\n*Multiplying the displayed difference by any uniformly bounded $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurable variable preserves the same estimate with its clearance indicator. To state the limiting consequence, let $\\mathsf E$ be a Polish space and let $e_\\delta$ be an $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurable $\\mathsf E$-valued variable. Suppose, for one fixed $s<-1$, that along a subsequence $$(e_\\delta,F_\\delta,R_\\delta)\\Longrightarrow(e,F,R)\n \\quad\\text{in }\\mathsf E\\times\\mathcal K(\\overline B_0)\n                   \\times H^s_{\\mathrm{loc}}(B_0),$$ where $\\mathcal K(\\overline B_0)$ is the space of nonempty compact sets with the Hausdorff metric. The limit $F$ is almost surely connected and contains $\\partial B_0$. Put $U=B_0\\setminus F$ and $$A_F=\\left\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}\\left(\\bigcup_i\\mathop{\\mathrm{supp}}f_i,F\\right)>0\\right\\}.$$ Then, almost surely, $$\\begin{split}\n &\\mathbf 1_{A_F}\\,\n \\mathbb E\\left[\\exp\\left(i\\sum_i u_iR(f_i)\\right)\n             \\,\\middle|\\,\\sigma(e,F)\\right]\\\\\n &\\qquad=\\mathbf 1_{A_F}\\,\n \\exp\\left(-\\frac1{2a^2}\n                \\sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_U(f_i,f_j)\\right).\n\\end{split}\n\\label{eq:conditional-flat-limit}$$ Thus, conditional on $\\sigma(e,F)$, the restrictions of $R$ to the component interiors of $U$ are independent zero-boundary GFFs divided by $a$, including components born from a pinched single precursor. This is first tested on deterministic compact buffers with positive limiting clearance and then extended by a countable exhaustion. The retained variable $e_\\delta$ may encode any exact-cut coordinates and flat constants for which this joint convergence holds; the constants are added after the centered assertion. Its $\\mathcal E_\\delta$-measurability excludes data from any later revelation.",

        "exact_quote": "In <a href=\"#eq:stopped-joint-extraction\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:stopped-joint-extraction\">[eq:stopped-joint-extraction]</a>, let $Q\\Subset D$ be compact.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-stopped-tvs",
        "exact_quote": "The wired boundary cluster converges jointly with $h_\\delta$, with its labels, to $A_{-a,a}(h)$. In a free flat parent, after subtracting its label and writing $f$ for the zero-boundary limiting remainder, the first odd carpet converges to $A_{-2a,2a}(f)$. At depth $r$, define the global closed carpet as the closed complement of the holes still unsearched after every branch has met $r$ odd rims; it includes all earlier layers and, in the wired case, the first wired layer. For each fixed finite $r$, this global carpet converges in ordinary Hausdorff distance to the corresponding canonical nested carpet. Its labels and restarted zero-boundary fields converge on every finite family of pointed compact buffers in the limiting holes. These pointed conclusions include distinct limiting components with the same discrete precursor; they do not assign one whole precursor carpet to several separate Hausdorff limits.",

        "exact_quote": "Consider a seed stop in an initial free parent of label $b_0$, or the composite wired stop defined above. The set $A$ is connected to the original boundary, and every component $O$ of $D\\setminus A$ is simply connected. Conditionally on $\\mathscr E$, $$h|_O=m_O+h^O,\\qquad m_O-b_0(O)\\in2a\\mathbb Z,\n \\label{eq:stopped-component-law}$$ where the $h^O$ are independent zero-boundary GFFs. Here $b_0(O)$ is the label of its initial parent chamber; it is $0$ in the initial free domain and $\\pm a$ in a wired hole. The labels are tight on every finite family of pointed components.*\n\n*On every compact subset of $D$ away from $W_0\\cup S$, $A$ has zero area and the full conditional mean $M$ is the locally integrable piecewise constant function $m_O$. Locally $M$ is the limit of the finite signed odd-hole contributions of the discovered clusters, with the initial parent label added. These statements hold for every member of a specified countable family of sweeps and observable indexed stops, each conditional only on its own retained state.*\n\n*For a composite wired stop, every $O$ is contained in one pointed limiting wired hole. Locally $M$ is the limit of the finite signed odd-hole contributions of the discovered clusters, with the initial parent label added. These statements hold for every member of a specified countable family of sweeps and observable indexed stops, each conditional only on its own retained state.*\n\n*For a composite wired stop, every $O$ is contained in one pointed limiting wired hole.         "exact_quote": "Let $f$ be a zero-boundary GFF in a bounded simply connected parent $P$. Suppose $$-p\\le c_H\\le q,\\qquad p,q>0,\\qquad p+q\\ge2\\lambda.$$ For these fixed $p,q$, suppose also that all $c_H$ lie in one fixed deterministic countable subset $\\mathcal L\\subset[-p,q]$. In each component with $-p<c_H<q$, insert $A_{-p+c_H,q-c_H}(f^H)$ in its zero-boundary remainder. Leave components already labelled $-p$ or $q$ untouched. The closed union is $A_{-p,q}(f)$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-canonical-geometry",
        "exact_quote": "In the free procedure of <a href=\"#def:free-procedure\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:free-procedure\">1</a> the retained sets form a countable family of pairwise disjoint connected compact sets, each strictly inside its parent domain. They and all their labelled holes are measurable functions of the GFF. Each retained cluster is the closure of the union of its odd-hole boundaries. Conditional on the unlabelled recursive geometry, including which odd holes belong to the same retained cluster, their relative jump signs are independent and fair.*\n\n*In a parent field $b+f$, a positive first-generation retained cluster is contained both in the positive excursion of $f$ and in the boundary-connected upper first-passage set of $f$ at level $2a$. The containing cable sets have paths respectively above $b$ and below $b+2a$ in total field units. A negative retained cluster satisfies the reflected containments, giving paths below $b$ and above $b-2a$. The carpet formed by continuing through even holes and stopping at first odd holes is $A_{-2a,2a}(f)$. These statements remain valid at $a=2\\lambda$.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $K\\Subset B\\Subset D$, with $B$ a regular polygon, and let $\\widetilde\\Phi_n$ be zero-boundary cable GFFs in the admissible approximations of $D$.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-local-kernel",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $K\\Subset B\\Subset P$ as above and a sequence of $[0,1]$-valued cable tests $T_n$ supported in $C_{K,n}$. There are a subsequence and a measurable $k$, with $0\\le k\\le1$, on continuum field restrictions to $B$, such that:*\n\n1.  *In the zero-boundary reference field in $P$, every joint limit along this subsequence satisfies $\\mathbb E[T\\mid\\Phi]=k(\\Phi|_B)$.*\n\n2.  *The same $k$ is the conditional kernel in every deterministic domain $D$ with $\\overline P\\subset D$, for the same cable tests in admissible approximations containing the identical subdivided $\\mathsf P_n$. For a prescribed harmonic mean, including a constant boundary value, require its ALS extended means to converge in $H^s(\\mathcal B)$ to the chosen full continuum ALS extension, and to converge smoothly on buffer neighborhoods in the interior finite-difference sense used below. Equivalently, for every bounded continuous field functional $v$, $$\\mathbb E[T_n v(\\widehat\\Phi_n)]\n           \\longrightarrow \\mathbb E[k(\\Phi|_B)v(\\Phi)]$$ along the selected subsequence. This convergence of mixed expectations does not require convergence of the tests as field functions.*\n\n3.  *Let a fixed random parameter $\\Theta$ select $D$ and its mean, and suppose that conditionally on $\\Theta$ the original total parent field $\\Phi_D$ has that GFF law. For every joint limit $$(\\Theta,\\widehat\\Phi_n,T_n)\n           \\ \\Longrightarrow\\ (\\Theta,\\Phi_D^{\\mathrm{aux}},T)$$ along the selected subsequence, the auxiliary field marginal satisfies $(\\Theta,\\Phi_D^{\\mathrm{aux}})\\stackrel{\\mathrm d}=\n      (\\Theta,\\Phi_D)$, and $$\\mathbf 1_{\\{\\overline P\\subset D\\}}\n     \\bigl(\\mathbb E[T\\mid\\Theta,\\Phi_D^{\\mathrm{aux}}]\n                      -k(\\Phi_D^{\\mathrm{aux}}|_B)\\bigr)=0.$$*\n\n\n*One subsequence works for any countable collection of tests, polygons, and thresholds. For the collar tests at $t\\in a\\mathbb Z$, write the selected kernels as $k_t^\\pm$.         "exact_quote": "The conclusions of [lem:reverse-buffer,lem:local-kernel] [lem:reverse-buffer](#lem:reverse-buffer), [lem:local-kernel](#lem:local-kernel), with the same reference kernel $k$, also hold for the following auxiliary approximations of a bounded simply connected domain $D$. Choose a fixed dyadic point $r\\in D$ and put $$V_n=\\bigl\\{v\\in\\varepsilon_n\\mathbb Z^2\\cap D:\n  \\text{a lattice path from \\(v\\) to \\(r\\) stays at distance\n  at least \\(\\varepsilon_n\\) from \\(D^c\\)}\\bigr\\}.$$ For sufficiently large $n$ this is the approximation of (Jego, Lupu, and Qian 2023, (2.6)) [[JLQ2023Fields](#ref-JLQ2023Fields)], translated to $r$. Use the cable realization of the vertex GFF killed on leaving $V_n$: every edge incident to $V_n$, including a full exit edge ending at an outside Dirichlet vertex, has its original resistance and its usual conditional Brownian bridge. Complete this cable function to the full grid in $\\mathcal B$ by setting missing vertices and missing edges identically to zero, and harmonically extend it into each grid face. Denote this extension by $\\widehat X_n$. The missing edges have deterministic zero traces, not additional Brownian bridges.*\n\n\n*For a simply connected regular polygon $B\\Subset D$, use the connected, hole-free complete-cell approximations $B_n^\\square$ and reveal all of $C_{B,n}$, including its perimeter cables. Extend the residual, zero on $C_{B,n}$, by the same completed-grid operator. The corresponding fields are tight in the fixed $H^s(\\mathcal B)$, $s<-1$.       "exact_statement": "The conclusions of [lem:reverse-buffer,lem:local-kernel] [lem:reverse-buffer](#lem:reverse-buffer), [lem:local-kernel](#lem:local-kernel), with the same reference kernel $k$, also hold for the following auxiliary approximations of a bounded simply connected domain $D$. Choose a fixed dyadic point $r\\in D$ and put $$V_n=\\bigl\\{v\\in\\varepsilon_n\\mathbb Z^2\\cap D:\n  \\text{a lattice path from \\(v\\) to \\(r\\) stays at distance\n  at least \\(\\varepsilon_n\\) from \\(D^c\\)}\\bigr\\}.$$ For sufficiently large $n$ this is the approximation of (Jego, Lupu, and Qian 2023, (2.6)) [[JLQ2023Fields](#ref-JLQ2023Fields)], translated to $r$. Use the cable realization of the vertex GFF killed on leaving $V_n$: every edge incident to $V_n$, including a full exit edge ending at an outside Dirichlet vertex, has its original resistance and its usual conditional Brownian bridge. Complete this cable function to the full grid in $\\mathcal B$ by setting missing vertices and missing edges identically to zero, and harmonically extend it into each grid face. Denote this extension by $\\widehat X_n$. The missing edges have deterministic zero traces, not additional Brownian bridges.*\n\n\n*For a simply connected regular polygon $B\\Subset D$, use the connected, hole-free complete-cell approximations $B_n^\\square$ and reveal all of $C_{B,n}$, including its perimeter cables. Extend the residual, zero on $C_{B,n}$, by the same completed-grid operator. Its covariance form $\\mathsf K_n^B$ and the full covariance form satisfy, for smooth tests $f,g$ on the box, $$\\operatorname{Cov}(\\widehat X_n(f),\\widehat X_n(g))\n       \\longrightarrow G_D(f,g),\\qquad\n \\mathsf K_n^B(f,g)\n       \\longrightarrow G_{D\\setminus\\overline B}(f,g),\n \\label{eq:killed-graph-green}$$ where the limiting kernels are zero-extended to $\\mathcal B$. The corresponding fields are tight in the fixed $H^s(\\mathcal B)$, $s<-1$. For a constant parent label $t$, add directly to $\\widehat X_n$ the chosen continuum ALS extension $u_t$: it equals $t$ on $\\overline D$, is harmonic on $\\mathcal B\\setminus\\overline D$, and is zero on $\\partial\\mathcal B$.",

        "exact_quote": "Every positive-diameter Hausdorff limit of lattice free-current clusters is one retained canonical cluster, and every retained canonical cluster is the limit of its visible precursor. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Free cluster procedure** ([source](#stmt-def-free-procedure)): For a zero-boundary GFF $f$ in a Jordan domain $O$, define $\mathcal F_a(f,O)$ recursively as follows.
- **Admissible approximation** ([source](#sec:lattice-domains)): An admissible approximation is a family of simple nearest-neighbor polygons $P_\delta$ in $\delta\mathbb Z^2$ such that their boundaries have parametrizations converging uniformly to a parametrization of $\partial D$, and every compact subset of $D$ eventually lies inside $P_\delta$.
- **Flat chamber** ([source](#sec:spatial)): A *flat chamber* means a component cut off by an open monochromatic $W$ perimeter, with its height on that perimeter fixed.
- **Matching wall** ([source](#subsec:auxiliary)): A *matching wall* means a revealed monochromatic open path or perimeter in the $W$-lattice.
- **Complete pattern** ([source](#pm-h-15)): A *complete pattern* in a finite vertex-and-edge set specifies all its $s$ spins and all its $W$ edge states.
- **Thin local set** ([source](#sec:local-sets)): It is *thin* when $h_A$ is integration against that harmonic function, with no further distribution supported on $A$.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **s-cuts** [claim](#stmt-lem-finite-cuts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-finite-cuts): Product edge weight and exact cut factorization. -> flat residual chambers
- **s-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prop-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-comparison): Griffiths inequalities and monotone coupling. -> positive association
- **s-circuits** [claim](#stmt-prop-circuits) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-circuits): Imported circuit bound with comparison and iteration over scales. -> buffered circuit bounds
- **s-collar** [claim](#stmt-lem-collar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-collar): Crosscut trimming, gap circuits and compactness. -> collar exclusion
- **s-counts** [claim](#stmt-prop-cluster-counts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cluster-counts): Seed exploration with collar separation. -> count tails
- **s-no-shadowing** [claim](#stmt-cor-indexed-no-shadowing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-indexed-no-shadowing): Collar windows at each stop and a union bound. -> no shadowing
- **s-pattern** [claim](#stmt-prop-pattern-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-pattern-comparison): Four monotone batches compared with circuit laws. -> pattern comparison
- **s-contiguity** [claim](#stmt-prop-full-contiguity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-full-contiguity): Terminal tail and witness events with pattern comparison. -> contiguity
- **s-spectral** [claim](#stmt-prop-plane-green) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-plane-green): Reflection positivity, Cauchy mixture and dispersion defect give the Green covariance. -> subsequential Green covariance
- **s-orthogonality** [claim](#stmt-prop-screened-orthogonality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-screen-bridge-coupling-2): Pattern moving, bridge coupling and transfer to flat domains. -> exterior orthogonality
- **s-wick** [claim](#stmt-prop-gaussian-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-gaussian-moments): Pole cancellation and maximum principle. -> Wick recursion
- **s-normalization** [claim](#stmt-prop-plane-normalization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-plane-normalization): Free-energy correspondence fixes the coefficient. -> multiplier
- **s-flat-gff** [claim](#stmt-thm-flat-gff) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-plane-normalization-2): Tightness, Green convergence and identified coefficient. -> flat-domain limit
- **s-stopped** [claim](#stmt-lem-stopped-full-field) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-stopped-full-field): Zero area by Fatou and buffer partition identification. -> stopped field and carpets
- **s-no-crossing** [claim](#stmt-prop-no-crossing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-no-crossing): Common local kernel calibrated in the parent, bounded in the stopped component. -> no crossing
- **s-partition** [claim](#stmt-prop-partition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-partition): No crossing, label recovery and sign correlation. -> visible partition
- **s-matching** [claim](#stmt-prop-complete-matching) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-complete-matching): Flat patch, Sierpinski partition and no-shadowing exclude invisible precursors. -> complete matching
- **s-main** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-complete-matching-2): Combine flat limit, carpets and matching. -> joint limit

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **inv-joint-limit**: On every bounded Jordan domain and every admissible polygonal approximation, the rescaled height and both current-cluster collections together with the distinguished boundary cluster converge jointly in law to the Gaussian free field divided by the stated constant, the two recursive collections built from that same field, and the canonical boundary two-valued set.
- **inv-height-topology**: The rescaled height converges in the local negative-order Sobolev topology for every exponent below the stated threshold, and the cluster collections converge in the positive-diameter matching topology.
- **inv-plane-normalization**: Along every subsequence considered, the plane covariance coefficient equals the reciprocal of the squared level parameter, fixed by the six-vertex free energy only after the Gaussian plane limit is established.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-area-measures**: Use the theorem to obtain limits of cluster area measures, magnetization fields, domain-wall curves or exact metric exponents. -> The theorem only covers the height and the compact supports of the clusters; nothing is asserted about measures or exponents.
- **anti-uniformity-near-one**: Quote constants uniformly in the parameter as the weight parameter approaches its upper endpoint. -> Constants may blow up; no uniform control is proved.
- **anti-non-jordan**: Apply the cluster convergence to unbounded domains or domains lacking admissible polygonal approximations. -> The approximation and boundary-parametrization hypotheses fail, so the identification does not apply.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The main results are non-constructive continuum scaling limits: convergence in law of lattice height and cluster collections to the Gaussian free field and canonical two-valued local sets, whose definition rests on continuum exploration of the field. No finite procedure with finite input and output computes them, so an executable reference with an independent oracle would not test any statement of the source.

<a id="pm-s5"></a>
## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The result is a continuum scaling-limit theorem for a fixed critical line. It gives no procedure with finite steps, so there is nothing to package as a library routine. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The limit object (a Gaussian free field with recursive two-valued local sets) could inspire procedural generation of nested random regions. The paper gives no discretised sampler and no error control, so it is only a loose analogy. |
| tools | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | No analysis tool, checker or converter follows from the statements. The proof relies on measure-theoretic and probabilistic arguments, with constants that depend on the fixed parameter. |
| algorithms | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The recursive free cluster procedure is defined on a continuum Gaussian field and exposes local sets that are measurable functions of the field. It is a mathematical definition, not a finite-step algorithm with a cost model. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The only structural notion is a locally finite family of compact sets under a matching metric, which is a topological device for stating convergence. It does not give an indexable or updatable container. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Nothing in the paper concerns dataflow, arithmetic units or memory layout. The lattice weights are used only inside proofs. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | No hardness assumption, adversary model or security property appears. The model is a spin and current ensemble studied for its scaling limit. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | A Gaussian free field appears as a limit law, but there is no learning problem, loss, generalisation statement or training procedure. The covariance is fixed by the model. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | There is no objective, constraint set or optimality claim. The paper explicitly disclaims uniformity in the parameter, so no tuning guarantee exists either. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Independence of residual chambers is a probabilistic fact about conditional laws, not a protocol, consensus or messaging structure. No communication model is present. |
| other | False | none | not_applicable | stated | The real consumer is mathematical physics: it supplies the joint scaling limit for height and cluster families under stated hypotheses. That is a theoretical contribution, and the theorem excludes area measures, magnetisation fields and domain-wall curves. |

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **lim-critical-line-fixed-parameters** (hypothesis): Every conclusion is proved for one fixed pair of coupling parameters on the self-dual critical line with the interaction parameter at most the coupling; all constants may depend on that fixed parameter. Blocked use: ['Applying the limit to off-critical, anisotropic or non-self-dual couplings', 'Reading the constants as universal across the critical line']
- **lim-no-uniformity-near-endpoint** (edge_case): No uniform control of the constants is claimed as the weight parameter approaches its upper endpoint, so error terms may degenerate there. Blocked use: ['Quoting error constants uniformly in the parameter as it approaches the upper endpoint', 'Interchanging the mesh limit with a limit in the parameter']
- **lim-bounded-jordan-admissible-domains** (hypothesis): The domain must be a bounded Jordan domain approximated by admissible nearest-neighbor polygons whose boundary parametrizations converge uniformly; the statement is not asserted outside this class. Blocked use: ['Applying cluster convergence to unbounded domains or multiply connected regions', 'Using approximations whose boundaries do not converge uniformly in parametrization']
- **lim-excluded-measures-and-curves** (formal_scope): The theorem concerns the height and the compact supports of clusters only; limits of cluster area measures, magnetization fields, spin domain-wall curves and exact metric exponents are explicitly not part of the result. Blocked use: ['Deducing limits of cluster area measures or magnetization fields from the theorem', 'Extracting domain-wall curve laws or fractal metric exponents from it']
- **lim-matching-topology-multiplicity** (formal_scope): Cluster collections converge only in the positive-diameter matching topology, in which the matching need not be one-to-one; multiplicities and singleton members are forgotten, so the limit does not control how many lattice clusters approximate a given limit cluster. Blocked use: ['Counting lattice clusters by counting limiting clusters', 'Using the metric to track individual clusters or their multiplicity across meshes']
- **lim-nonconstructive-recursive-procedure** (nonconstructive): The limiting cluster collections are defined by a recursive procedure on a continuum Gaussian field using canonical two-valued local sets; this is a measurable-function definition with no finite-step procedure or cost model. Blocked use: ['Treating the free cluster procedure as terminating pseudocode with a running time', 'Packaging the definition as a ready-to-run sampler with error guarantees']
- **lim-no-conditioning-on-completed-history** (edge_case): Estimates controlling the production of a cut are averaged over the exploration and are not asserted after conditioning on a completed stopping history; only residual fields may be conditioned on stopping data, and only when the estimate is uniform over the residual class. Blocked use: ['Conditioning the count or circuit estimates on a fully revealed stopping history', 'Using averaged exploration bounds as pathwise bounds for a given completed cut']
- **lim-contiguity-excludes-wired-component** (edge_case): Full-spin contiguity between flat-chamber and plane laws is stated for flat domains with free complementary components and does not cover a fixed-color wired component before its removal. Blocked use: ['Transferring small plane probabilities to the original wired current before its boundary cluster is exposed']
- **lim-formal-verification-status** (unknown): No machine-checked formalization of the result or its comparator is available in the provided material. Blocked use: ['Citing the theorem as formally verified']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For each fixed point on the critical Ashkin–Teller line, including the four-state Potts endpoint, we prove the conjectured joint scaling limit of the height and both current-cluster collections in every bounded Jordan domain, for every admissible polygonal approximation. The height converges to a Gaussian free field with the predicted coupling constant, and the clusters converge to canonical recursive two-valued local sets of that same field. The joint limit includes all nesting depths and the distinguished wired boundary cluster.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

The Ashkin–Teller model originates in the four-component lattice model of Ashkin and Teller (Ashkin and Teller 1943) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[AshkinTeller1943](#ref-AshkinTeller1943)]. Its current representation raises a geometric question beyond convergence of the associated height: what is the joint continuum law of all primal and dual current clusters, and how are these collections coupled to the field? We prove the joint limit in <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a> for every fixed point on the critical line, including the four-state Potts endpoint. This is the height and current-cluster assertion formulated by Alcalde López, Heeney, and Lis (Alcalde López, Heeney, and Lis 2026, Conjecture 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[AlcaldeLopezHeeneyLis2026](#ref-AlcaldeLopezHeeneyLis2026)].

Fix $J>0$ and $U\le J$ with $\sinh(2J)=e^{-2U}$. Our zero-boundary Gaussian free field has covariance $2\pi(-\Delta_D)^{-1}$, with logarithmic singularity $-\log|z-w|$. In this normalization put $$\lambda=\frac\pi2,\qquad a=\lambda\sqrt g,\qquad
 g=\frac8\pi\arcsin\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+e^{4U}}}{2}\right).$$ Thus $4/3<g\le4$ and $\lambda<a\le2\lambda$. For the wired current, the first limiting cluster is the symmetric two-valued local set with labels $\pm a$. For the free current, first expose $\mathrm{CLE}_4$ holes and retain an asymmetric two-valued split inside each hole; repeat in all complementary components. Both constructions use the same field. The theorem retains every nesting depth and the distinguished wired boundary cluster. It includes tightness and identification of the entire compact supports in positive-diameter Hausdorff matching topology.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### Prior work and the scope of the result

The finite spin, percolation, and height representation used here is due to Lis (Lis 2022b, secs. 1.1–1.3 and 2.2) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Lis2022Spins](#ref-Lis2022Spins)]; his current expansion (Lis 2022a, sec. 2) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Lis2022Boundary](#ref-Lis2022Boundary)] gives the precise odd/even-edge weights. A noncrossing primal–dual contour representation appears earlier in Rys (Rys 1963, sec. 3) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[Rys1963](#ref-Rys1963)]. We recall and verify the finite coupling, including its boundary convention, in <a href="#sec:model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:model">2</a>.

At $U=0$, the currents are double random currents and $g=2$. Duminil-Copin and Lis (Duminil-Copin and Lis 2019, Theorems 1.1–1.2) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[DuminilCopinLis2019](#ref-DuminilCopinLis2019)] identified the finite signed nesting field with a dimer height. Duminil-Copin, Lis, and Qian (Duminil-Copin, Lis, and Qian 2025) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[DRC2025](#ref-DRC2025)] established conformally invariant limits for the nesting field and recursive cluster-boundary families. Their introductory statements cover Jordan domains, while the detailed joint boundary-family Theorems 6.2 and 6.4 assume a $C^1$ boundary and use injective matching of loops. Alcalde López, Heeney, and Lis (Alcalde López, Heeney, and Lis 2026, Theorem 1.14 and Appendix B) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[AlcaldeLopezHeeneyLis2026](#ref-AlcaldeLopezHeeneyLis2026)] state the joint limit of the height and both complete compact current-cluster collections in Jordan domains, using the noninjective positive-diameter matching topology considered here. Their Conjecture 1.2 asks for the critical-line extension obtained by replacing $\sqrt2$ with $\sqrt g$.

Alcalde López and Sepúlveda (Alcalde López and Sepúlveda 2026, Theorems 1.4 and 9.5, and Lemma 9.1) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[AlcaldeLopezSepulveda2026](#ref-AlcaldeLopezSepulveda2026)] study a stronger joint decomposition at the Ising point involving the XOR field, cluster measures, and signs, with the Gaussian field identified with the nesting height. Their introductory theorem is stated for Jordan domains; their detailed joint convergence theorem adds a boundary Minkowski-dimension hypothesis. Those additional field and measure limits are outside our statement. Our conclusion concerns the height and complete current supports for every fixed $4/3<g\le4$.

The analytic input is related to the six-vertex model with weights $(1,1,c)$, where $c=\sqrt{1+e^{4U}}\in(1,2]$. Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Lammers, and Manolescu (Duminil-Copin et al. 2026) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[DKLM2026](#ref-DKLM2026)] prove a height scaling limit for $\sqrt3\le c\le2$ and establish several inputs on the larger interval $1\le c\le2$: logarithmic bounds for even increment moments, one-parity spin-percolation circuits, a specified flat-exhaustion plane law, and a free-energy identification of the normalization conditional on a Gaussian plane limit. Odd plane correlations vanish by height reversal. We use these larger-range results. The covariance, screening, and Gaussianity arguments needed for the whole interval are given here; the free-energy formula is applied only after its convergence premise has been established. A related full-plane height theorem for the balanced six-vertex state is proved in (OpenAI 2026b, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[BalancedSixVertex2026](#ref-BalancedSixVertex2026)]. Its unit height corresponds to $K=2H$ here, and its multiplier $1/\arcsin(c/2)$ agrees with ours after this normalization. This comparison does not replace the local Gaussianity proof or the random-domain and cluster identifications below.

For the reflection argument, coordinate and diagonal tests for six-vertex weights already appear in (Fröhlich et al. 1980, sec. 6) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[FrohlichIsraelLiebSimon1980](#ref-FrohlichIsraelLiebSimon1980)]. We use the general reflection-positive framework of (Fröhlich et al. 1978) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[FrohlichIsraelLiebSimon1978](#ref-FrohlichIsraelLiebSimon1978)]; for the reflected Hilbert-space construction and positive-transfer representation, see (Usui 2012, secs. 3.1–3.3 and 4.1) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[Usui2012](#ref-Usui2012)]. The height transfer in (Duminil-Copin et al. 2026, sec. 4.5.3) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[DKLM2026](#ref-DKLM2026)] is a closer model-specific precedent and permits negative one-step spectrum. The transfer, screening, and collision strategy also has a related implementation for integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data in (OpenAI 2026a, secs. 5, 7, and 9–10) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[Triangular](#ref-Triangular)]. We prove the square-frame and random-chamber arguments required here.

The continuum identification uses thin two-valued local sets (Aru, Sepúlveda, and Werner 2019; Aru and Sepúlveda 2018) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[ASW2017](#ref-ASW2017), [AS2018](#ref-AS2018)], first-passage sets (Aru, Lupu, and Sepúlveda 2020a, 2020b) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[ALS2017](#ref-ALS2017), [ALS2018](#ref-ALS2018)], and the canonical excursion decomposition (Aru, Lupu, and Sepúlveda 2023) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[ALS2023](#ref-ALS2023)]. The recursive exploration and thinness architecture also follows the double-current work (Duminil-Copin, Lis, and Qian 2025) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[DRC2025](#ref-DRC2025)]. In the present coupling, we must additionally identify which discrete odd holes belong to a single current cluster, exclude macroscopic pieces invisible to those holes, and compare passage tests after a second coupled random exploration. We prove these steps with the conditioning and approximation hypotheses stated in the corresponding propositions. A proof strategy follows the formal theorem in <a href="#subsec:proof-strategy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="subsec:proof-strategy">2.7</a>.

<a id="sec:model"></a>
### The model and the limiting objects

<a id="sec:lattice-domains"></a>
#### Parameters and lattice domains

Fix real numbers $J>0$ and $U\leq J$ satisfying $$\sinh(2J)=e^{-2U}.$$ Throughout the proof these parameters remain fixed. Put <a id="eq:parameters"></a>$$\label{eq:parameters}
 t=(1+e^{4U})^{-1/2},\qquad c=t^{-1},\qquad
 \theta=\arcsin(c/2),\qquad g=\frac{8\theta}{\pi}.$$ Then $1/2\leq t<1$, $1<c\leq2$, and $4/3<g\leq4$. The value $U=0$ gives $g=2$; the endpoint $J=U=(\log3)/4$ gives $g=4$. Constants below may depend on the fixed parameter. We make no claim of uniformity as $t\uparrow1$.

Let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded Jordan domain. An admissible approximation is a family of simple nearest-neighbor polygons $P_\delta$ in $\delta\mathbb Z^2$ such that their boundaries have parametrizations converging uniformly to a parametrization of $\partial D$, and every compact subset of $D$ eventually lies inside $P_\delta$. Let $G_\delta=(V_\delta,E_\delta)$ contain all lattice vertices and edges on or inside the polygon, and let $B_\delta$ be its boundary-cycle edges. The weak dual $G_\delta^\dagger$ has a vertex at each bounded-face center and an edge across each edge of $E_\delta\setminus B_\delta$. We draw all primal and dual edges as straight segments. Boundary contraction will be used only to describe current weights, not when drawing clusters.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
#### The coupled currents and their height

We use the spin–edge–height construction of (Lis 2022b, secs. 1.1–1.3) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[Lis2022Spins](#ref-Lis2022Spins)], with its wired/free boundary specialization made explicit below. Sample spins $$\tau:V_\delta\longrightarrow\{-1,1\},\qquad
 \tau^\dagger:V(G_\delta^\dagger)\longrightarrow\{-1,1\},$$ with $\tau=1$ on $P_\delta$. For each mutually dual pair $e=uv$, $e^\dagger=ff'$, impose <a id="eq:spin-constraint"></a>$$\label{eq:spin-constraint}
 (\tau(u)-\tau(v))(\tau^\dagger(f)-\tau^\dagger(f'))=0.$$ Give an admissible pair weight <a id="eq:spin-weight"></a>$$\label{eq:spin-weight}
 t^{N(\tau)+N(\tau^\dagger)},$$ where $N$ counts nearest-neighbor disagreements on the respective graph. No boundary constraint is imposed on the dual spins.

Conditional on the spins, all edges of $B_\delta$ are primal open. For each remaining mutually dual pair, independently of the other pairs, use the following rule:

<div class="center">

| Spin information                     | Primal/dual open states | Probabilities  |
|:-------------------------------------|:------------------------|:---------------|
| $\tau^\dagger(f)\ne\tau^\dagger(f')$ | $(1,0)$                 | $1$            |
| $\tau(u)\ne\tau(v)$                  | $(0,1)$                 | $1$            |
| Neither disagreement                 | $(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)$     | $1-t,1-t,2t-1$ |

</div>

The constraint makes the first two rows mutually exclusive. Denote the resulting edge sets by $\widehat n_\delta$ and $\widehat n_\delta^\dagger$. Their open edges never cross. Both may be closed at a mutually dual pair; the two currents are not generally complementary.

<a id="eq:current-weight"></a>
After contracting the wired boundary and deleting its cycle edges, the primal odd edges are those crossing dual spin disagreements. The other primal open edges are even. In the current expansion of (Lis 2022a, sec. 2, Equations (2)–(3) and Proposition 1) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[Lis2022Boundary](#ref-Lis2022Boundary)], their law specializes to $$\label{eq:current-weight}
 \mathbb P(n_{\rm odd},n_{\rm even})\ \propto\
 2^{k(n_{\rm odd}\cup n_{\rm even})}
 x^{|n_{\rm odd}|}y^{|n_{\rm even}|},
 \qquad
 x=1,\quad y=c-1,$$ with $n_{\rm odd}$ Eulerian and disjoint from $n_{\rm even}$. Here $k$ includes isolated vertices. To check the weight directly, an odd edge contributes $t$, an even edge contributes $1-t$, and a closed primal edge contributes $t$, after summing its possible dual states. The common factor is $t^{|E_\delta\setminus B_\delta|}$, leaving $((1-t)/t)^{|n_{\rm even}|}$. The primal colors are constant on open components and give $2^{k-1}$ choices with the wired color fixed. An admissible Eulerian odd set determines the dual colors up to a common flip. These graph-dependent constant factors yield <a href="#eq:current-weight" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:current-weight">[eq:current-weight]</a>. The same calculation gives free boundary conditions for the dual current. In the original parameters, $$x=e^{2U}\sinh(2J)=1,\qquad
 y=e^{2U}\cosh(2J)-1=\sqrt{1+e^{4U}}-1.$$ It is the spin-and-edge construction above, not just <a href="#eq:current-weight" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:current-weight">[eq:current-weight]</a>, that specifies the joint law.

<a id="eq:height-increments"></a>
Set $H_\delta=0$ on $P_\delta$, and define corner increments by $$\label{eq:height-increments}
 H_\delta(f)-H_\delta(v)=\frac12\tau(v)\tau^\dagger(f)
 \quad\text{when \(v\) is incident to \(f\)}.$$ The circulation around an interior primal edge is $$\frac12(\tau(u)-\tau(v))
              (\tau^\dagger(f)-\tau^\dagger(f'))=0.$$ All boundary primal increments are zero. Since the polygon is simple, these elementary circuits generate the corner graph’s cycle space, so <a href="#eq:height-increments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:height-increments">[eq:height-increments]</a> defines a unique height. It is integer-valued on primal vertices and half-integer-valued at face centers. We also use $$K_\delta=2H_\delta.$$ Thus a nearest corner increment of $K_\delta$ has magnitude one. Conversely, the spins are recovered from its residues, up to a common sign $\varepsilon$, by $$\tau(v)=\varepsilon(-1)^{K_\delta(v)/2},\qquad
 \tau^\dagger(f)=\varepsilon(-1)^{(K_\delta(f)-1)/2}.$$ Around a corner-lattice plaquette there are six possible increment patterns. The two patterns with both opposite diagonals flat have spin weight $1$; the other four have weight $t$. Dividing by the common factor $t$ gives the six-vertex weights $(1,1,c)$, with $c=1/t$; see also (Lis 2022b, sec. 2.2, Corollary 2.5) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[Lis2022Spins](#ref-Lis2022Spins)]. The corner lattice is a fixed rotation and dilation of the square lattice. This local identification, together with the infinite-volume identification recalled in <a href="#sec:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:spectral">4</a>, is what permits the six-vertex estimates used below. As a distribution on $D$, the height is <a id="eq:height-smearing"></a>$$\label{eq:height-smearing}
 H_\delta(\varphi)=\delta^2
       \sum_{v\in V_\delta}H_\delta(v)\varphi(v),
 \qquad \varphi\in C_c^\infty(D).$$ This is an atomic distribution, which belongs locally to $H^s$ for $s<-1$. Interpolated heights used in intermediate estimates will be compared with this precise smearing.

Let $\mathcal C_\delta^{\rm w}$ be the collection of all connected components of the primal open subgraph, including its boundary component $C_{\partial,\delta}$, and let $\mathcal C_\delta^{\rm f}$ be the collection of all dual open components. A component includes its vertices and drawn edges. We retain components at every nesting depth.

<a id="subsec:auxiliary"></a>
#### An auxiliary representation

When analyzing one of the two currents, denote it by $N$, and denote its exact dual complement by $W$. This complement is an auxiliary spin percolation, not the other current of the joint sample. The spin constant along $W$ is called $s$, and the spin constant along $N$ is called $d$. At an ambiguous pair, $W$ is open with probability $t$, whereas the other current is open with probability $1-t$.

A *matching wall* means a revealed monochromatic open path or perimeter in the $W$-lattice. Its connections in the revealed region are retained as boundary connections; separate appearances of the same connected perimeter are not treated as unrelated wires. For a free current, the complementary $W$-percolation is wired. The finite cut law in <a href="#lem:finite-cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:finite-cuts">4</a> explains why the height in a component behind a matching wall has constant boundary data. All conditional comparisons below refer to this representation.

The same cut law gives the vocabulary for nesting. A hole of a free $N$ component is *odd* when its adjacent $s$ spin differs from the adjacent exterior $s$ spin of that component. Crossing the component changes $K_\delta$ by $2$ times one relative sign in every odd hole, and by zero in every other hole. Conditional on $(N,s)$, these signs are independent and fair for distinct free components. After the wired boundary component is exposed, each residual chamber carries a free same-parity current; the value of $K_\delta$ on its component-side $W$ perimeter is $+1$ or $-1$ relative to the original boundary height. The edge factor and the jump identity proving these statements are given in <a href="#lem:finite-cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:finite-cuts">4</a>.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### Continuum normalization and two-valued sets

Let $h$ be the zero-Dirichlet GFF in $D$ with covariance $$G_D=2\pi(-\Delta_D)^{-1}.$$ Thus $G_D(z,w)=-\log|z-w|+O(1)$ near the diagonal. Set <a id="eq:normalization"></a>$$\label{eq:normalization}
 \lambda=\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad
 a=\sqrt g\,\lambda,\qquad
 a^2=2\pi\arcsin(c/2).$$ In particular $\pi/\sqrt3<a\leq\pi$, so $\lambda<a\leq2\lambda$. A zero-boundary GFF in an open subdomain is always extended by zero when viewed as a distribution on a larger domain.

We use the canonical thin two-valued local set $A_{-\alpha,\beta}(f)$ of a zero-boundary GFF $f$, with $\alpha,\beta>0$ and $\alpha+\beta\geq2\lambda$. It includes the domain boundary. The conditional harmonic function on each complementary component is either $-\alpha$ or $\beta$; after subtracting that value, the field in the component is an independent zero-boundary GFF. These sets are measurable functions of the field. We use their uniqueness, monotonicity, and Jordan-hole properties with the hypotheses stated in <a href="#sec:local-sets" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:local-sets">7</a>; see (Aru, Sepúlveda, and Werner 2019; Aru and Sepúlveda 2018; Aru, Lupu, and Sepúlveda 2020a) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[ASW2017](#ref-ASW2017), [AS2018](#ref-AS2018), [ALS2017](#ref-ALS2017)]. In particular the complementary loops of $A_{-2\lambda,2\lambda}$ have law $\mathrm{CLE}_4$.

<a id="stmt-def-free-procedure"></a>
<div id="def:free-procedure" class="definition">

**Definition 1** (Free cluster procedure). For a zero-boundary GFF $f$ in a Jordan domain $O$, define $\mathcal F_a(f,O)$ recursively as follows.

1.  Expose $A_{-2\lambda,2\lambda}(f)$. In every complementary component $V$, write its label as $\xi\,2\lambda$, $\xi\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $f_V$ be the zero-boundary remainder.

2.  If $\xi=1$, retain $A_{-2\lambda,2a-2\lambda}(f_V)$ as one cluster. If $\xi=-1$, retain $A_{-(2a-2\lambda),2\lambda}(f_V)$. The retained set includes its outer boundary $\partial V$.

3.  In each complementary component of the retained set, subtract its conditional harmonic value and repeat the procedure with the zero-boundary remainder.

Keep all retained clusters from all recursive generations. The $\mathrm{CLE}_4$ set exposed in the first step is not itself retained.

</div>

If this procedure is invoked above an incoming flat value $b$ of the original field, the CLE component has absolute label $b+\xi2\lambda$ and the retained split has absolute labels $b$ and $b+\xi2a$. We call the holes with the nonzero jump relative to this incoming value $b$ *odd holes*. The use of this term in lattice explorations is consistent with the jump decomposition proved below.

Define $$\mathcal C^{\rm f}=\mathcal F_a(h,D).$$ For the wired collection, first retain $$C_\partial=A_{-a,a}(h),$$ and apply $\mathcal F_a$ to the zero-boundary remainder in every complementary component of $C_\partial$, retaining all resulting clusters together with $C_\partial$. Denote that collection by $\mathcal C^{\rm w}$. Both constructions use the *same* $h$, including the canonical choices of all its local sets. This defines their joint coupling. The all-generation local finiteness needed below is proved in <a href="#cor:canonical-local-finiteness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:canonical-local-finiteness">59</a>, rather than assumed as part of the definition.

<figure id="fig:free-procedure">

<figcaption>One recursive step of the free construction. Only the split inside a CLE hole is retained as a current cluster. For the wired construction, the boundary set $A_{−a, a}$ is retained first.</figcaption>
</figure>
